family: Execution and cost tactics at daily-rebalance scale (rebalance bands / signal hysteresis, slower rebalance H, netting, passive limit ladders vs taker, hour-of-day choice, constant-$ vs hold-shares accounting) applied to the trader/ trend book
thesis: The tactic is to turn the record's assumed 21 bp/side (taker16 + slip5, trader/config.py:135) into a realized number and to cut the number of times it is paid: (i) stop paying for sign flips that carry no information (a Schmitt-trigger/hysteresis band on the 30-day return, or a 3-day stride), (ii) pay maker instead of taker fees by posting at the touch with a 24 h deadline and crossing the remainder, (iii) execute in the liquid UTC window instead of at 00:00 UTC, (iv) choose deliberately between constant-$ (1/n) rebalancing and hold-shares, whose drift turnover the record never charged. Every one of these draws on exactly one of the four no-free-lunch sources: REDUCED REALIZED COST. None creates drift: net_t = gross_t − turn_t·c (trader/backtest.py:188-190), and the family only shrinks turn_t·c. The record's own structural fact makes the ceiling small and computable: the book's 0.155/day turnover is essentially all sign flips (analytic zero-crossing rate of a 30-day moving sum, 0.165/day, matches the measured 0.152–0.162), and the whole cost stack is worth 0.18–0.20 Sharpe on the 2018–2025 PIT book (gross +0.74 vs net@21 +0.56, POWERED_RESULT.md:57) and nothing on 2024–2026, where the gross itself reads ≈0 to −1.5. The one component that is not pure cost — constant-$ vs hold-shares — is a rebalancing effect the record has measured at ±1 Sharpe in BEAR22 (830 SPEC.md:95-98), but it is a bet on within-position trend persistence and is flagged as forecast-shaped, not claimed as a tactic. Honest summary: this family is the cost module of a controller (TASK_915's Λ calibration), not a line that can reach the goalposts by itself.
math:
CONSTRUCTION (trader/strategy.py:60-77, 123-154; backtest.py:224): pos[t,i] = s_i(t)/n_present(t), s = sign(logC_t − logC_{t−30}); turn_t = Σ_i |pos_t − pos_{t−H}|. A sign flip costs 2/n; a universe change (Δn=±1) costs ≈ 2/(n+1) once; a |Δpos|<0.2% band (config.py:128) is inert because the smallest flip is 2/273 = 0.73% (PIT) or 2/39 = 5.1% (survivor universe).

TURNOVER DECOMPOSITION (analytic, to be measured by the kill experiment): for a moving sum of L iid Gaussian daily increments, P(sign change over a stride of h days) = arccos(ρ)/π with ρ = (L−h)/L. L=30, h=1: ρ = 29/30 → arccos(0.9667)/π = 0.0824 flips/asset/day → expected flip turnover/day = n · 0.0824 · 2/n = 0.165, independent of n. Measured: 0.155 (PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md:36), 0.162 (20-asset cell), 0.152 PIT FULL (POWERED_RESULT.md:57). Residual for renormalisation from universe changes: ≤ 0.01/day (<5%); the small shortfall below 0.165 is trend persistence (positive autocorrelation lowers crossing rates). h=2: ρ=0.9333 → 0.1169 per 2 d → 0.117/day (−25%). h=3: ρ=0.9 → 0.1436 per 3 d → 0.0957/day (−38%; ≈35×/yr vs 56.6×). h=5: ρ=0.8333 → 0.1864 per 5 d → 0.0746/day (−52%). Hysteresis at ±θ on the 30-day return (θ in units of σ_S = σ_daily·√30): fraction of zero-crossings that reach ±θ before re-crossing ≈ E[one-step overshoot]/θ with one-step std = σ_daily·√2 = 0.258 σ_S → θ = 0.5σ_S removes roughly 40–50% of flips, θ = 1σ_S roughly 70–75% (heuristic; simulate/measure, do not assume).

COST PER BP AND SHARPE SLOPE: annual turnover T_a = 56.6 (survivor) / 55.5 (PIT) → cost/yr = T_a·c·1e-4 = 0.566%/yr per bp; 21 bp → 11.89%/yr (PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md:79), 11.65% PIT (POWERED_RESULT.md:88). Book vol from the record's own tier spread: net@8 − net@21 = 1.09 − 0.97 = 0.12 for Δcost = 13·56.6 bp = 7.36%/yr → σ_book ≈ 61%/yr (cross-check: ln(21.69)/4.6 yr = 0.669/yr log-return at Sharpe 1.09 → daily σ 3.21% → 61%). PIT: 0.67 − 0.56 = 0.11 for 7.2%/yr → σ ≈ 66%. Hence ΔSharpe per bp of realized per-side cost = 0.0085–0.0093. 21→10 bp: +0.09 to +0.10; 21→5: +0.14 to +0.15; 21→0: +0.18 to +0.20 (= gross − net@21 = 0.74 − 0.56 on PIT, exactly the whole stack).

CEILING BY COMPOSITION: H=3 (turnover ×0.62) with realized c ≈ 12 bp (blended maker/taker, below) → drag 55.5·0.62·12 bp = 4.1%/yr, saving 7.5%/yr → +0.11 → PIT net ≈ +0.67. Add θ=0.5σ_S (flips ×0.55 on top) → drag ≈ 2.3%/yr → +0.14 → PIT ≈ +0.70. The gross bound is +0.74 (net@0, POWERED_RESULT.md:57); the bar is +0.97; PIT CI [−0.13,+1.23] at 21 bp and [−0.01,+1.34] at 8 bp both straddle 0. On 2024–26: PIT gross BULL24 +0.13, CHOP25 +0.22 (POWERED_RESULT.md:55-56); 2026H1 net@8 −1.659 (LEDGER row 898) → gross ≈ −1.5; c → 0 cannot change the sign. Note the survivor H=3 row's +0.38 net@21 uplift (0.97→1.35, PORTFOLIO_RESULT.md:68) exceeds its cost-only component (+0.07 from 38% less turnover at 21 bp); the other +0.3 is a gross path change from sampling every third day — unreplicated on PIT, treat as luck until measured.

FEE/SPREAD ARITHMETIC (Kraken schedule effective 2026-07-09, fetched): maker/taker by 30-day volume: $100k+ 0.12/0.25; $250k+ 0.10/0.22; $500k+ 0.08/0.20; $1M+ 0.06/0.18; $2.5M+ 0.04/0.15; $5M+ 0.02/0.12; $10M+ 0.00/0.10 (tier 1 is 0.40/0.80). Monthly volume of this book = 0.155·30·book = 4.65·book, so the record's taker16 presumes the $1–2.5M/month band → book ≈ $215k–540k; below ~$100k of book the honest taker fee is 22–38 bp and the whole record is optimistic. Maker−taker gap at the relevant tiers: 10–13 bp/side. Spread on majors from the 907 fixture (2026-08-27 20:49Z, wire_fixture_kraken_v2_2026-08-27.jsonl): ETH/USD 2505.81/2505.97 = 0.64 bp full spread (record median 0.11 USD = 0.44 bp; frozen 0.01 = 0.04 bp), BTC/USD 79989.2/79989.3 = 0.0125 bp; top-of-book size ETH 0.35–5.1 ETH ($0.9k–$12.8k), BTC 0.4/0.27 BTC ($32k/$21k) → a $2.5–10k clip (1–2% of a $250–500k book) crosses at ≈0–1 bp slippage on majors, so 'slip5' is 5–400× the major-pair half-spread and is only defensible as an alt-weighted guess (alt spreads are not in the DB; assumption 5–50 bp).

RECOVERABLE RANGE (assumptions: $250–500k book, 64 assets, 1–2% clips, post at touch, 24 h deadline, remainder crossed): majors 21 → 5–7 bp (maker 4–6 + spread/AS ±1) ≈ 65–75% recovered; alts 21 → 10–20 bp ≈ 5–50%; 1/n blend where alts dominate the count: 21 → 10–14 bp ≈ 33–50% recovered → +0.06 to +0.10 Sharpe at the slope above.

UNCHARGED DRIFT TURNOVER: regime_series charges only Σ|target_t − target_{t−H}|; holding 1/n dollar weights requires daily trades ≈ Σ_i w_i|r_i − r_p| ≈ 0.8·σ_xs,daily; at 3–4% daily cross-sectional dispersion this is 2.4–3.2%/day = +9–12×/yr on top of 55.5 → +1.9–2.5%/yr at 21 bp → −0.03 to −0.04 Sharpe not in any published number (hold-shares avoids it but changes gross: 830 SPEC.md:95-98).

TIMING RISK OF INTRADAY PATIENCE: the traded slice is 0.155 of gross; delaying it half a day adds variance ≈ 0.155²·0.5·σ_mkt,d² = 0.024·0.5·0.03² ≈ 1.1e-5 vs σ_book,d² ≈ 1.0e-3 → ~1% variance, ~0.5% Sharpe dilution; zero expected cost because the book has no intraday forecast.

MEMO CORRECTION: lore/fable_direction_memo_2026-09-03.md:174-186 states a 5 vs 10 bp adverse-selection difference is '≈0.3–0.5 Sharpe-points/yr' on a 60%-vol book; the arithmetic is 5 bp · 56.6 = 2.8%/yr ÷ 0.61 = 0.046 Sharpe — the memo overstates by ~8–10×; its qualitative conclusion (second-order) stands a fortiori.

bear_positive_without_forecast.argument: Execution and turnover tactics have identically zero drift: net_t = gross_t − turn_t·c (trader/backtest.py:188-190) and the family only shrinks the second term. The sign of the bear P&L is inherited from the gross book, which is the 30-day sign rule's forecast (BEAR22 gross +1.22 PIT, POWERED_RESULT.md:57; 2026H1 gross ≈ −1.5 from LEDGER 898's net@8 −1.659). Cutting c from 21 to 0 bp on the 2026H1 book moves it by at most +0.2 and leaves it deeply negative; on BEAR22 it was positive before any tactic. The only component with a gross effect — constant-$ (1/n) rebalancing vs hold-shares, measured at BEAR22 gross +1.218 vs +0.225 in 830/E0 (experiments/830_corridor/SPEC.md:95-98) — is positive in a bear precisely because re-shorting a winning short is a bet on trend persistence inside the position; that is a forecast dressed as accounting, and the honest classification is that BEAR-positivity is not obtainable from this family without one.

literature.ref: Magill & Constantinides 1976, 'Portfolio selection with transactions costs', J. Economic Theory
literature.claim: Under proportional costs the optimal policy is a no-trade region: do nothing while the portfolio is inside it, trade minimally to its boundary when outside — the theoretical basis for bands/hysteresis rather than continuous rebalancing.
literature.numbers: No numbers used; qualitative structure only.

literature.ref: Davis & Norman 1990, 'Portfolio selection with transaction costs', Mathematics of Operations Research 15(4)
literature.claim: Rigorous free-boundary (HJB) solution of the Merton problem with proportional costs; optimal strategy keeps the risky fraction inside a wedge and trades only at its edges (minimal trading).

literature.ref: Gârleanu & Pedersen 2013, 'Dynamic Trading with Predictable Returns and Transaction Costs', Journal of Finance 68(6):2309-2340
literature.claim: Closed-form dynamic policy under quadratic costs: aim in front of the target, trade partially toward the aim, weight slower-decaying signals more; commodity-futures implementation beats naive benchmarks net of costs. Relevant here as the controller TASK_915 already adopts; this family supplies its realized cost parameter Λ.

literature.ref: Almgren & Chriss 2000, 'Optimal Execution of Portfolio Transactions', Journal of Risk 3(2)
literature.claim: Mean-variance execution: trade schedule trades permanent/temporary impact against timing risk; with negligible impact (our $2.5-10k clips vs eight- to nine-figure daily volume) the AC optimum is immediate execution — AC therefore does NOT justify patience here; the case for patience must come from fee/spread capture, which AC does not model.

literature.claim: Liquidation with limit orders: choose posting depth δ against fill intensity λ(δ) under non-execution risk and price risk, with a terminal market order at the deadline; usable 'to liquidate over a few hours' — the correct frame for a pre-decided daily trade list executed passively with a deadline.

literature.ref: Cartea, Jaimungal & Penalva 2015, 'Algorithmic and High-Frequency Trading', Cambridge UP (execution-with-limit-orders chapters)
literature.claim: Limit-order execution balances fast fill against adverse selection: fill probability is highest exactly when price is about to move through you; deadline forces market orders; latency erodes the value of imbalance signals — distinguishes informed (897-type) from uninformed passive execution.

controllability: Maximal, and that is the family's real merit. The policy is a deterministic pipeline with four scalar knobs: decision hour (00:00 UTC vs a 13-17 UTC boundary), stride H ∈ {1,2,3,5}, hysteresis θ on the 30-day return, and an execution schedule (post at touch for T hours, cross the remainder). Action space per asset per day is {hold, flip long↔short, enter/exit}, with turnover bounded by construction at 2/n per flip and an optional hard daily cap; every order is explainable ex post from (signal value, θ, prior position, fill log), and the realized cost is a per-fill ledger quantity, not an assumption. Auditability matches the record's existing gate discipline (unmodified cell_metrics scorer, seed 819, n_boot 2000). What is lost: (a) any gross uplift — the family cannot add drift, so 'better hold on policy' here means a cheaper and more stable book, not a more profitable signal; (b) the ability to react intraday (the trade list is frozen at the decision time; timing risk is ~1% variance, negligible); (c) at hysteresis θ ≥ 1σ the book holds stale signs longer and the BEAR22 short entries arrive later — a measurable gross cost, not a free lunch; (d) passive fills on alts are uncertain, so realized cost is stochastic and must be reported as a distribution per liquidity tier, not a constant.
compute: Zero GPU, on either host. The H × θ × accounting sweep is trader/ numpy on the existing PIT daily panel (runs/819_single_asset/_close_pit_daily.npz, extended via ohlcv_daily): 819 Phase 2 scored 8 cells in 24 s, so 48 cells × 4 tiers × 3 accounting modes is minutes of CPU inside the standard safe_run wrapper on gpu-server. The 907 read is a pre-registered read of an artifact the factory is already producing (B2 row); no new capture. Engineering: ≤150 LOC (hysteresis signal variant + drift-inclusive turnover accounting + hold-shares gross) outside the parity path, ~1-2 engineer-days. The operator's 64 GB GPUs are irrelevant to this family; stating that plainly is part of the answer.

kill_experiment.design: Pre-registered 48-cell grid on the PIT 273-asset daily panel 2018-10→2026-06 (dead coins included, 819 POWERED builder): H ∈ {1,2,3,5} × hysteresis θ ∈ {0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0}·σ̂_S (σ̂_S = causal trailing-30d daily vol × √30; θ=0 reproduces the frozen 819 rule bit-for-bit as the parity check) × accounting ∈ {as-shipped target-weight turnover; drift-inclusive turnover (charge Σ_i|w_i(1+r_i)/(1+r_p) − w_i| every day held); hold-shares (no drift trades, gross from share holdings)}. Score each cell at c ∈ {5, 8, 12, 21} bp with the unmodified trader.backtest.cell_metrics (seed 819, n_boot 2000), by regime and by calendar year (2024, 2025, 2026H1 separately), Bonferroni over 48. Additionally report the turnover decomposition per cell: flip share, renormalisation share, drift share. Second leg, zero compute: pre-register a read of the 907 B2 artifact's estimand-1 median and p90 at 5m and 1h for ETH/SOL/XRP (BTC only if its frozen-mid runs clear D77) as the realized adverse-selection input for majors, and its touch/trade-cross fill bounds as the optimistic fill-rate input.

honest_odds: P(this family alone clears the goalposts — unseen years, net@21 ≥ +0.97 with CI lo > 0, BEAR-positive, ≥3 seeds) ≈ 0-2%. Reasoning: the family's ceiling is the gross of whatever book it executes; on the only cost-honest PIT read that gross is +0.74 over 2018-2025 (below the +0.97 bar even at zero cost) and ≈0 to −1.5 on 2024-2026H1 (POWERED_RESULT.md:55-57; LEDGER 898). At 0.0085-0.0093 Sharpe per bp of realized cost and a 38-55% turnover cut, the mechanically available uplift is +0.10 to +0.15, which cannot bridge either gap. P(the family delivers ≥ +0.10 net Sharpe on top of any gross that exists) ≈ 60-70% — the fee gap (10-13 bp/side) and the H=3/hysteresis turnover reduction are arithmetic, not hypotheses; the uncertainty is alt fill rates and the uncharged drift turnover (−0.03 to −0.04) partially offsetting it. P(the H/θ path changes gross by more than ±0.2 on PIT) ≈ 25%, and if it does it is a forecast-shaped effect that needs its own panel, not a tactic. Net: worth running as a CPU-minutes cost module for TASK_915's controller; not worth a queue row as a direction.
open_doubts: The flip/renormalisation decomposition (≈95/5) is analytic, not measured; the kill experiment must print it. Trend persistence and the present-mask flicker on dead coins could shift it a few percent either way.

Alt spreads on Kraken are not in the repo (the DB has no quotes) and the literature read gives only qualitative rankings; the 'slip5' baseline and the 10-20 bp alt estimate are assumptions. Uncharged drift turnover of the constant-$ book (estimated +9-12×/yr, −0.03 to −0.04 Sharpe at 21 bp) has never been measured; if daily cross-sectional dispersion is above 4% the record's turnover is understated by >20%.

Hold-shares vs constant-$ changed BEAR22 gross by ~1 Sharpe in 830/E0 (+0.225 vs +1.218); whether that is a genuine within-position rebalancing effect or a bet on trend persistence is undetermined, and it is the one lever in this family that could masquerade as edge.

The survivor H=3 result (+1.35 vs +0.97 net@21) is n=1 on a survivor universe with unmeasured turnover; +0.3 of it is unexplained by cost and must be treated as luck until the PIT sweep reproduces it across H ∈ {2,3,5}.

Kraken's July-2026 schedule qualifies tiers by 30-day volume OR assets-on-platform; the realized maker/taker tier for a $250-500k book depends on which qualifies and is an operator fact, not a repo fact.

907's touch-conditional markouts are an optimistic bound on adverse selection and say nothing about queue position; the true passive fill rate over a 24 h deadline on alts is unknown and is the main uncertainty in the 33-50% recoverable range.

The direction memo's '0.3-0.5 Sharpe-points/yr for 5 vs 10 bp adverse selection' (memo:1.4) is arithmetically ~0.05; the planner should correct it in the record so the second-order argument is not later read as first-order.

Moving the daily boundary from 00:00 UTC to ~13-17 UTC changes which 30-day returns the sign rule sees; a trend rule is nominally time-of-day invariant (819 Phase 1 found duration invariance), but the PIT gross at a different boundary has never been measured and could move by sampling noise of the same order as the H=3 surprise.

Everything above is scoped to the trend book because it is the only cost-honest book in the record; if TASK_915's G-A passes, the family's numbers must be recomputed at that book's turnover, which under GP partial trading will be lower than 55×/yr and will shrink the cost stack further.
